hero.title: Morning News & Global Update — Sunday 15 November 2026
hero.description: ASEAN diplomacy, Ukraine negotiations, Iran and Hormuz security, Gaza, Nigeria's 2027 election disputes, Africa's mining tensions, North American trade and Europe's AI ambitions.
hero.marquee: ASIA: ASEAN summit opens in Manila | UKRAINE: Zelensky says US raised Donbas-for-NATO question | MIDDLE EAST: Hormuz shipping remains at risk | NIGERIA: INEC says it will obey court orders on Atiku's eligibility | CANADA: Carney reports progress in US trade talks | EUROPE: AI investment gap debated

morningSummary: Sunday's global agenda is dominated by diplomacy and the consequences of unresolved conflicts. ASEAN leaders are meeting in Manila from 15 to 17 November, with the South China Sea and Myanmar's civil conflict high on the agenda. In Europe, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says US negotiators raised a possible withdrawal from parts of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership; no agreement has been reached, and a large prisoner exchange remains under discussion. In the Middle East, uncertainty over the Iran conflict continues to threaten shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while hospital officials in Gaza report new deaths in Jabaliya despite a fragile ceasefire. In North America, Canada's Mark Carney says trade talks with Donald Trump are progressing, but there is no signed deal. Nigeria's 2027 political landscape remains shaped by the ADC leadership dispute and INEC's promise to obey binding court orders; the commission also faces more than 300 pending lawsuits. In Guinea, authorities report at least 10 deaths during clashes linked to an illegal-mining crackdown. European leaders are debating how to close the AI investment and infrastructure gap. RadiantWaves distinguishes official statements, allegations and independently confirmed facts, and will update developing reports as stronger evidence becomes available.
breaking: ASIA / ASEAN — The 49th ASEAN Summit opens in Manila, with the South China Sea, Myanmar's conflict and regional security on the agenda.
UKRAINE — Zelenskyy says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave parts of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership; no agreement has been reached.
MIDDLE EAST — AP reports continuing uncertainty over Iran diplomacy and claims of tanker mine incidents near the Strait of Hormuz; details require independent confirmation.
GAZA — Hospital officials say an Israeli drone strike killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya; Israel says it targeted Hamas militants.
CANADA / US — Mark Carney says trade talks with Donald Trump are progressing, but no final agreement has been announced.
NIGERIA / ADC — INEC chairman says the commission will obey binding court decisions concerning Atiku Abubakar's eligibility; this is not a final ruling on eligibility.
NIGERIA — INEC says it is dealing with more than 300 pending court cases as preparations for the 2027 election continue.
GUINEA — Authorities report at least 10 deaths and 13 injuries in clashes during a security operation against unauthorised mining.

featured.title: ASEAN Summit Opens in Manila as Regional Leaders Face Maritime and Humanitarian Crises
featured.summary: The 49th ASEAN Summit begins on 15 November with the South China Sea, Myanmar's conflict and regional security at the centre of discussions.
featured.content:
Leaders and senior representatives from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and partner countries are gathering in Manila for the 49th ASEAN Summit and related meetings, scheduled from 15 to 17 November. The agenda includes the South China Sea, the conflict in Myanmar, regional economic cooperation and the wider impact of wars in the Middle East and Ukraine. The Philippines is hosting the summit as ASEAN chair.

The bloc is expected to review implementation of its Five-Point Consensus on Myanmar, which calls for an end to violence, dialogue among all parties, humanitarian access and the appointment of an ASEAN special envoy. Myanmar's military authorities remain excluded from high-level political participation because the bloc says progress on the peace plan has been inadequate.

On the South China Sea, ASEAN and China continue work towards a Code of Conduct. Negotiators have made progress, but the agreement is not expected to be concluded at this summit. Competing maritime claims and incidents at sea remain a test of regional diplomacy and international law.

WHY IT MATTERS: The summit brings together countries whose trade routes, energy supplies and security are closely connected. A failure to manage maritime disputes peacefully could increase the risk of confrontation and disrupt global shipping. Myanmar's crisis also continues to displace civilians and undermine regional stability.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the summit communiqué, commitments on humanitarian access in Myanmar, progress reports on the South China Sea Code of Conduct and the arrival of major external partners. US President Donald Trump is expected to join later meetings in Manila, while China's Premier Li Qiang is attending the ASEAN sessions.
featured.source: Associated Press (15 November 2026); Bernama (14 November 2026); ASEAN summit announcements

topStories.title: Zelensky Says US Raised Possible Donbas Withdrawal in Exchange for NATO Membership
topStories.summary: Ukraine's president says US negotiators asked whether Kyiv would leave the parts of Donbas it still controls in return for NATO membership. No agreement has been reached.
topStories.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says US negotiators raised a possible trade-off under which Ukraine could withdraw from the parts of the eastern Donbas region it still controls in exchange for NATO membership. The question followed the latest US-brokered talks with Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi. It is a reported negotiating proposal, not an agreed settlement or an announced change in Ukraine's policy.

The talks ended without a ceasefire or breakthrough on territory. Zelenskyy said the sides had made progress towards a large prisoner exchange involving more than 1,000 people, although final numbers and arrangements were still being discussed. Territorial control, security guarantees and the role of European countries remain unresolved.

Ukraine has consistently rejected Russian demands that it surrender territory. Moscow continues to claim the Donbas, while Kyiv argues that any settlement must respect Ukraine's sovereignty and provide credible protection against renewed aggression. European governments have also pressed for a meaningful place in negotiations because they are major supporters of Ukraine's defence and reconstruction.

WHY IT MATTERS: A territorial concession tied to NATO membership would reshape European security and could set a precedent for how borders are negotiated after military aggression. The legitimacy of any settlement will depend on Ukraine's participation and the terms accepted by its people.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for clarification from Washington, Kyiv and NATO; confirmation of the prisoner exchange; and whether European representatives participate directly in the next round. No territorial agreement should be reported as final unless all parties formally confirm it.
topStories.source: Reuters (14 November 2026); Deutsche Welle (14 November 2026); statements by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy

topStories.title: Iran War Uncertainty Keeps Strait of Hormuz Shipping at Risk
topStories.summary: Conflicting signals from Washington and Tehran have stalled efforts for an interim agreement. Reports of tankers striking naval mines add to concern around one of the world's most important energy routes.
topStories.content:
Diplomatic efforts to stabilise the conflict involving Iran remain uncertain after US President Donald Trump sent mixed signals about whether Washington wants an interim agreement. The Associated Press reports that Qatar-led efforts to reopen a path to a deal have stalled, while the United States maintains economic and maritime pressure. US officials say Washington remains open to an agreement under acceptable terms; Tehran says it is willing to negotiate but has set conditions that include an end to hostilities and sanctions relief.

The Strait of Hormuz remains strategically sensitive because a substantial share of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments normally passes through the waterway. AP has also reported Iranian state television claims that three oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire near the strait. Those details have not been independently established in the report and should be treated as claims pending further confirmation.

The dispute has implications beyond the Gulf. Higher shipping insurance, rerouted vessels and uncertainty over energy supplies can raise costs for import-dependent economies, including countries in Africa and Asia. Oil exporters may benefit from higher prices, but consumers and governments that subsidise fuel can face larger bills.

WHY IT MATTERS: The security of Hormuz affects energy prices, shipping, inflation and the foreign-policy calculations of major powers. A renewed escalation could have global economic consequences.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Monitor verified maritime incident reports, statements from the relevant naval authorities, oil and shipping movements, and any concrete diplomatic proposal. Distinguish official claims from independently confirmed events.
topStories.source: Associated Press (15 November 2026); statements by US and Iranian officials; maritime incident claims reported by Iranian state television

topStories.title: Israeli Drone Strike Kills Two Palestinians in Jabaliya, Hospital Officials Say
topStories.summary: Hospital officials say two Palestinians were killed in a drone strike in northern Gaza. Israel says it targeted two Hamas militants; the wider ceasefire remains fragile.
topStories.content:
Hospital officials in Gaza say an Israeli drone strike killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya in northern Gaza and wounded several others. Israel said the strike targeted two Hamas militants. The accounts describe the parties' positions; independent details about the circumstances and the identities of those killed remain limited in the available reporting.

The incident comes amid continued casualties despite a ceasefire. Gaza's Health Ministry says at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, while the overall death toll from Israel's offensive has exceeded 74,600. These are figures issued by the ministry and should be attributed as such. Families are also continuing to recover and identify people killed during the war, with many remains still believed to be under rubble.

The humanitarian situation remains severe, with damaged homes, health facilities, water systems and limited access to essential services. A ceasefire can reduce large-scale fighting but does not by itself resolve the questions of civilian protection, reconstruction, governance, aid access and long-term security.

WHY IT MATTERS: Repeated violence threatens the durability of the ceasefire and deepens an already grave humanitarian emergency. Civilian protection and reliable humanitarian access remain central obligations under international law.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for independent verification of the strike, further statements from the Israeli military and Palestinian health authorities, and evidence of sustained aid access and compliance with ceasefire arrangements.
topStories.source: Associated Press (15 November 2026); Gaza Health Ministry; Israeli military statement

topStories.title: Carney Says Canada and US Make Progress on Trade Deal but No Agreement Yet
topStories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says talks with US President Donald Trump have advanced after lengthy discussions in the Philippines. Key details remain unresolved.
topStories.content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada and the United States are making progress towards a trade agreement after what he described as lengthy and substantive discussions with US President Donald Trump. Carney made the remarks while visiting the Philippines and taking part in meetings with Southeast Asian leaders. No final agreement has been announced.

The talks are taking place as Canada seeks to diversify trade and strengthen links with Asia-Pacific economies while preserving access to its largest export market, the United States. Carney also said Canada would not leave NATO and argued that the security arrangements for a free Europe should be determined by Europeans and NATO, not Russia.

For businesses, uncertainty over tariffs, market access and supply chains can affect investment decisions, manufacturing costs and employment. A negotiated settlement could reduce uncertainty, but the actual impact will depend on the text, sectors covered and enforcement arrangements.

WHY IT MATTERS: Canada-US trade is deeply integrated, particularly in energy, vehicles, agriculture and manufacturing. A deal could influence prices and investment on both sides of the border and signal the direction of North American economic relations.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for a published negotiating framework, confirmation of any tariff changes and details on the sectors included. Until the governments announce a signed agreement, the talks should be described as progress in negotiations, not a completed deal.
topStories.source: Reuters (14 November 2026); statements by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney

topStories.title: ADC Leadership Dispute: INEC Says It Will Obey Court Orders on Atiku's Eligibility
topStories.summary: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says the commission will comply with binding court decisions. The statement does not itself decide Atiku Abubakar's eligibility or resolve the ADC dispute.
topStories.content:
Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission is facing more than 300 pending court cases as preparations for the 2027 general election continue. INEC chairman Professor Joash Amupitan said the commission would obey any court order concerning former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar's eligibility to contest the presidency. He made the remarks while speaking at Chatham House in London.

The statement comes amid the legal dispute over the leadership of the African Democratic Congress. A Federal High Court judgment delivered on 5 November nullified the emergence of the David Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under it, including steps connected to Atiku's intended nomination. INEC has previously said it needed the certified judgment and legal advice before deciding what action to take.

The ADC has criticised the ruling and indicated it will pursue legal remedies. Those are the party's stated intentions; the legal outcome will depend on filings, court directions and any appeal. The commission's promise to obey court orders should not be misrepresented as a declaration that Atiku is either eligible or ineligible.

WHY IT MATTERS: The dispute affects opposition-party organisation, candidate selection and confidence in the electoral process. With more than 300 cases pending, timely judicial decisions and transparent INEC procedures are important to avoid uncertainty as the election timetable advances.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for formal appeal documents, any application for a stay, further court orders and INEC's written position after reviewing the certified judgment. RadiantWaves will distinguish the court's actual orders from party statements and political commentary.
topStories.source: The Guardian Nigeria (12 November 2026); PUNCH (11 November 2026); INEC chairman's remarks at Chatham House

topStories.title: INEC Faces More Than 300 Court Cases as 2027 Election Preparations Intensify
topStories.summary: The electoral commission says it is handling more than 300 pending lawsuits and is preparing a nationwide mock exercise scheduled for 28 November.
topStories.content:
Nigeria's electoral preparations are unfolding alongside a large volume of litigation. INEC chairman Joash Amupitan has disclosed that the commission is facing more than 300 pending court cases, while assuring that the commission will comply with binding judicial decisions. The cases cover different electoral and institutional issues; the figure should not be read as 300 cases relating to one party or one candidate.

INEC is also expected to conduct a nationwide mock election exercise on 28 November ahead of the 2027 general election. The exercise is intended to test elements of the electoral process, including accreditation and the use of election technology. Its value will depend on transparent reporting of test results, identified weaknesses and corrective action.

The commission's credibility will be judged not only by its technology but also by voter registration, logistics, security, accessible polling arrangements, transparent result management and equal treatment of political parties. Political actors have a responsibility to pursue disputes through lawful channels and avoid inflammatory claims that could undermine public confidence.

WHY IT MATTERS: Electoral litigation and technical readiness can shape trust long before polling day. Voters need clear information about what is being tested, what the test reveals and how identified problems will be addressed.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for INEC's detailed mock-election plan, the locations and procedures for the exercise, the publication of results and any subsequent court decisions affecting party leadership or candidate selection.
topStories.source: The Guardian Nigeria (12 November 2026); Nigeria Info FM news archive (14 November 2026); INEC statements

topStories.title: At Least 10 Killed in Guinea Clashes During Illegal-Mining Crackdown
topStories.summary: Guinean authorities say 10 people died and 13 were injured during a security operation in the northeastern gold-mining area of Balato. A judicial investigation is under way.
topStories.content:
Guinea's authorities say at least 10 people were killed and 13 injured during clashes in Balato, in the country's northeastern gold-mining region, during a security patrol targeting unauthorised mining. The government says protesters blocked the patrol with barricades and that the confrontation escalated into gunfire. Officials have not established in the available account who fired first. Five of those killed were described as unidentified foreign nationals.

The unrest reportedly involved burned vehicles and the theft of a firearm and a motorcycle. Judicial authorities are investigating the circumstances and responsibility. The crackdown forms part of a wider campaign against unauthorised mining, which the government says damages farmland and pollutes rivers.

Artisanal and small-scale mining is also an important source of income for many households. Enforcement that does not address livelihoods, local employment, environmental damage and the role of larger operators risks creating further tensions in communities that depend on mining.

WHY IT MATTERS: Guinea's mineral wealth is central to its economic future, but mining governance must protect workers, communities and the environment. The use of force and the deaths require an impartial investigation.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the judicial findings, identification of victims, any arrests or official disciplinary action and details of how the government intends to regulate mining while protecting local communities.
topStories.source: Associated Press (14 November 2026); statements by Guinean authorities

topStories.title: European Leaders Debate How to Close the AI Investment and Infrastructure Gap
topStories.summary: At a Dublin summit, EU leaders discussed investment, computing capacity and safeguards as Europe seeks to compete with the United States and China in artificial intelligence.
topStories.content:
European leaders and technology specialists used a summit in Dublin on 13 November to discuss how the continent can strengthen its artificial-intelligence capabilities while maintaining safety, accountability and public trust. Participants included Mistral AI chief executive Arthur Mensch and AI researcher Geoffrey Hinton. The debate focused on investment, access to computing infrastructure, chips, data centres and the adoption of AI across European industries.

Le Monde reports that European leaders are concerned about reliance on foreign digital infrastructure and the gap between Europe and the United States and China in developing frontier AI systems. Mensch argued that Europe should both build advanced models and accelerate AI adoption across its economy. The European Commission has estimated that at least €500 billion is needed for AI development and adoption, while proposals for AI mega-factories and other infrastructure remain subject to funding and implementation decisions.

The debate is especially relevant to France, which is seeking to position its technology sector as part of a more autonomous European digital economy. Investment alone, however, will not resolve questions about energy demand, skills, copyright, data protection, labour-market disruption and the concentration of market power.

WHY IT MATTERS: AI infrastructure is becoming an economic and strategic asset. Countries that lack computing capacity and skilled workers may become dependent on a small number of overseas providers.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the EU's funding decisions, the next budget negotiations, the proposed industrial adoption roadmap and concrete plans for AI infrastructure. Public safeguards and measurable productivity gains will be as important as headline investment figures.
topStories.source: Le Monde (14 November 2026); European Commission estimates and summit reporting

topStories.title: US FAA Ground Stop Lifted After Communications Disruption Affected Air Traffic Control
topStories.summary: A nationwide ground stop was issued on 13 November after telecommunications instability affected multiple air-route control centres. The FAA and transport officials said the restriction was lifted while the cause remained under investigation.
topStories.content:
The US Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on 13 November after communications problems affected multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centres. The FAA said technicians were investigating the issue and described its initial information as preliminary. The US Department of Transportation later said intermittent telecommunications outages had affected the stability of communications and radar systems used by air traffic control. The nationwide restriction was lifted.

The disruption caused delays and interruptions across the aviation network. Flights already airborne were handled under safety procedures, while departures were held and airlines worked to rebook passengers. Officials have not, in the cited updates, provided a complete technical explanation of the underlying failure or a final assessment of its cause.

The incident highlights the dependence of modern aviation on resilient communications and radar infrastructure. A disruption affecting several control centres can have consequences far beyond the location where a technical fault begins, particularly when aircraft and crews are operating across a tightly connected national network.

WHY IT MATTERS: Aviation safety depends on reliable communications, redundancy, tested contingency procedures and timely public information. The event also raises questions about investment in critical infrastructure and the ability to recover quickly from system failures.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the FAA's technical findings, any recommendations for system upgrades and information about how airlines are clearing the backlog. The ground stop has been lifted; do not describe it as still in force.
topStories.source: Federal Aviation Administration (13 November 2026); US Department of Transportation (13 November 2026)

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Monitor verified maritime incident reports, statements from the relevant naval authorities, oil and shipping movements, and any concrete diplomatic proposal. Distinguish official claims from independently confirmed events.
usaNews.source: Associated Press (15 November 2026); statements by US officials

leadersWatch.title: Leaders Watch
leadersWatch.description: Profiles of political and institutional leaders whose decisions are shaping international affairs. Reports distinguish confirmed decisions from political statements, allegations and unresolved legal questions.

leaders.name: Donald Trump
leaders.headline: Iran diplomacy and the Manila summit put US foreign policy under scrutiny
leaders.report: The US administration is sending mixed signals about the route to an interim agreement with Iran. Trump is also expected to join ASEAN-related meetings in Manila later in the summit period.
leaders.background: Washington is balancing military pressure, energy security, negotiations and strategic competition in the Indo-Pacific.
leaders.implications: The credibility of US diplomacy will depend on clear objectives and whether talks reduce escalation risks.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Watch for concrete agreements and independently confirmed outcomes, not announcements alone.

leaders.name: Emmanuel Macron
leaders.headline: France's AI ambitions form part of a wider European push for digital autonomy
leaders.report: European leaders and technology figures debated investment, infrastructure and AI safeguards at a Dublin summit. France is seeking a stronger role in Europe's technology ecosystem.
leaders.background: The debate takes place amid concerns about reliance on foreign digital platforms and the scale of investment needed to build European capacity.
leaders.implications: France's influence will depend on investment, skills, energy infrastructure and effective European cooperation.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Digital sovereignty should be measured by accessible infrastructure, responsible innovation and benefits for workers and businesses.

leaders.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
leaders.headline: INEC's legal workload and 2027 preparations keep electoral credibility in focus
leaders.report: INEC says it is facing more than 300 pending lawsuits and will obey binding court decisions. The commission is also preparing a nationwide mock exercise scheduled for 28 November.
leaders.background: The 2027 process includes party leadership disputes, election technology tests, voter registration, funding and security concerns.
leaders.implications: Public confidence will depend on transparent procedures and equal application of the law.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Assess the government and electoral institutions through measurable safeguards and published evidence.
leaders.source: The Guardian Nigeria; Nigeria Info FM; INEC

leaders.name: Atiku Abubakar
leaders.headline: INEC says Atiku's eligibility will be governed by binding court decisions
leaders.report: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says the commission will obey court orders concerning Atiku's eligibility. The statement does not itself determine the legal outcome of the ADC dispute.
leaders.background: The Federal High Court judgment affecting the David Mark-led ADC leadership and decisions taken under it remains subject to further legal process.
leaders.implications: Appeals and further court directions may affect the party's route to candidate selection.
leaders.radiantWavesView: The public deserves precise reporting: a party's intention to appeal is not the same as a court decision, and INEC's statement is not a final eligibility ruling.

leaders.name: Mark Carney
leaders.headline: Canada reports progress in trade talks with the United States
leaders.report: Carney says discussions with Donald Trump have been substantive and that progress is being made, but no final trade agreement has been signed.
leaders.background: Canada is also strengthening economic links with ASEAN and other Indo-Pacific partners.
leaders.implications: The final terms could affect North American supply chains, investment and jobs.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Judge progress by the signed text, tariff details and practical impact on businesses and households.

leaders.name: Vladimir Putin
leaders.headline: Ukraine negotiations remain blocked by territory and security guarantees
leaders.report: US-brokered talks have not produced a ceasefire. Zelenskyy says Washington raised the possibility of a Donbas withdrawal linked to NATO membership.
leaders.background: Russia maintains territorial claims rejected by Kyiv; the terms of any settlement remain unresolved.
leaders.implications: Moscow's position will shape whether talks move beyond limited humanitarian arrangements.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Any settlement should be judged by its terms, implementation and respect for Ukraine's sovereignty.

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.headline: China's regional diplomacy is in focus as ASEAN leaders meet in Manila
leaders.report: China's Premier Li Qiang is attending ASEAN sessions, while negotiations on a South China Sea Code of Conduct continue. The summit is not expected to conclude the code.
leaders.background: Maritime claims, trade, supply chains and strategic competition shape China's relations with Southeast Asian states.
leaders.implications: A peaceful maritime framework is important for regional stability and global commerce.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Monitor the actual commitments in summit documents and maritime conduct, not diplomatic language alone.

leaders.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
leaders.headline: Zelenskyy rejects assumptions that Ukraine has agreed to territorial concessions
leaders.report: The Ukrainian president says US negotiators asked about a possible Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO membership. No agreement has been reached.
leaders.background: Ukraine continues to seek security guarantees and meaningful participation in negotiations affecting its territory.
leaders.implications: The terms and legitimacy of any peace settlement will shape European security for years.
leaders.radiantWavesView: A durable settlement requires Ukraine's meaningful participation and verifiable protection for civilians and sovereignty.

leaders.name: Ursula von der Leyen
leaders.headline: EU debates the funding and safeguards needed to compete in artificial intelligence
leaders.report: European leaders are considering investment in computing capacity, chips and industrial AI adoption while maintaining risk oversight.
leaders.background: Europe has strong research and industrial capabilities but remains dependent on overseas digital infrastructure.
leaders.implications: Budget decisions will influence Europe's technological competitiveness and strategic autonomy.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Funding commitments need delivery plans, accountability and protections for public trust.

leaders.name: Andy Burnham
leaders.position: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.headline: UK-EU reset proposals remain a live issue in British political debate
leaders.report: Recent UK political debate has focused on whether closer practical agreements with the EU could reduce costs and red tape. Negotiations and final policy decisions must be followed through official announcements.
leaders.background: Trade, youth mobility, food standards and regulatory cooperation remain areas of discussion.
leaders.implications: Any agreement could affect business access, mobility and the UK's economic relationship with Europe.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Judge proposals by published agreements and their effects on households and businesses.
leaders.source: The Guardian; UK and EU public statements

leaders.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leaders.headline: African economic resilience remains exposed to global energy and trade shocks
leaders.report: African economies face uneven effects from energy-market disruption and trade-route uncertainty, while Guinea is seeking investment in infrastructure linked to its mineral resources.
leaders.background: Commodity dependence, financing costs and infrastructure gaps shape the continent's economic outlook.
leaders.implications: Regional cooperation and transparent resource governance are central to turning mineral wealth into public benefit.
leaders.radiantWavesView: African growth should be measured by jobs, local value addition, public services and environmental protection.

leaders.name: Marine Le Pen
leaders.headline: French opposition positioning continues as debates over public spending and civil society intensify
leaders.report: The National Rally's proposals on public funding for non-profit organisations remain part of a wider debate about the role of civil society, public money and political accountability.
leaders.background: French political competition is developing ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with public finances and institutional checks among the contested issues.
leaders.implications: Proposals affecting associations and public-interest organisations could have consequences for civic space and service provision.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Political proposals should be examined through their legal text, funding impact and effects on independent civic organisations.

UKRAINE — Zelenskyy says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave parts of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership; no agreement has been reached.
MIDDLE EAST — AP reports continuing uncertainty over Iran diplomacy and claims of tanker mine incidents near the Strait of Hormuz; details require independent confirmation.
GAZA — Hospital officials say an Israeli drone strike killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya; Israel says it targeted Hamas militants.
CANADA / US — Mark Carney says trade talks with Donald Trump are progressing, but no final agreement has been announced.
NIGERIA / ADC — INEC chairman says the commission will obey binding court decisions concerning Atiku Abubakar's eligibility; this is not a final ruling on eligibility.
NIGERIA — INEC says it is dealing with more than 300 pending court cases as preparations for the 2027 election continue.
GUINEA — Authorities report at least 10 deaths and 13 injuries in clashes during a security operation against unauthorised mining.

NIGERIA / ENERGY — Five new CNG stations have been commissioned in Lagos. Their stated capacity is about 8,400 vehicles daily at full operation; the government has not confirmed a uniform ₦340 selling price at the new sites.
breakingHistory.status: Developing — actual prices, supply and throughput require monitoring

breakingHistory.headline: GLOBAL DIPLOMACY — The White House says Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin plan to meet in Shenzhen next Thursday during APEC. US officials say expectations for immediate agreements are limited.

CANADA — Prime Minister Mark Carney says trade negotiations with the United States are progressing, but no agreement has been reached. Canada is also pursuing trade arrangements with ASEAN and the Philippines.

NIGERIA / ADC — The African Democratic Congress is considering its next legal steps after receiving a certified judgment affecting its leadership structure and the process behind Atiku Abubakar’s nomination. Further court proceedings may change the position.
FRANCE — The National Rally’s proposals to restrict public funding for some non-profit organisations have prompted concern about the independence of civil society and public-interest groups.
GLOBAL / CLIMATE — UN Secretary-General António Guterres says immediate and drastic emissions cuts are needed to avert the most catastrophic effects of climate change.
TECHNOLOGY — Microsoft says services affected by a global outage, including Teams and Outlook, have been restored.
EUROPE — German lawmakers have voted to expand the powers of the country’s foreign intelligence service, prompting debate about security powers and oversight.
GUINEA — Authorities say at least 10 people were killed and 13 injured in clashes during a security patrol targeting unauthorised gold mining in Balato. A judicial investigation is under way.

NIGERIA — Investigative journalist Daniel Ojukwu has been ordered to remain in custody until a December 1 bail hearing in a cybercrime case linked to his reporting. The allegations are before the courts.

NIGERIA / ADC — The ADC is considering its next legal steps after receiving a certified judgment affecting its leadership structure and the process that produced Atiku Abubakar's nomination. Further court proceedings may change the position.

NIGERIA — Atiku Abubakar has criticised the Tinubu administration over insecurity, citing October deaths and displacement figures. The figures are attributed to his campaign statement and require comparison with underlying monitoring data.
FRANCE — Marine Le Pen's National Rally is proposing major restrictions on public funding for some non-profit organisations, prompting debate about civil society and institutional checks.
UNITED STATES — A telecommunications outage affecting FAA air-route control centres caused a nationwide ground stop and widespread delays. Officials say the cause remains under investigation.

todaysBigQuestion: When peace negotiations involve territory, security guarantees and the future of millions of people, who should decide what compromises are acceptable — and what safeguards are needed to protect civilians and sovereignty?
thoughtForToday: Diplomacy is measured not by the number of meetings held, but by the lives protected and the promises that are honoured.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: RadiantWaves Perspective: Diplomacy Must Protect People, Sovereignty and Accountability
radiantWavesPerspective.content: Today's developments show how closely security, economic stability and public trust are connected. ASEAN's discussions on Myanmar and the South China Sea will matter only if they help prevent violence and protect lawful maritime activity. Ukraine's future cannot be settled through assumptions or proposals presented as agreements; the country affected must participate meaningfully in decisions about its territory and security. In the Middle East, claims about maritime incidents and military operations require independent verification, while civilian protection and humanitarian access must remain central. In Nigeria, electoral institutions must explain their decisions clearly and obey binding court orders without prejudging unresolved cases. RadiantWaves will continue to distinguish confirmed facts, official statements, allegations and analysis, and will correct or update reports when reliable new evidence becomes available.
